title: Stop LearningOrderRepositoryImpl.getOrder from writing to the DB as a side effect of a FutureProvider build call
rule: SM-2 (provider build is pure — no writes/side effects)
why: getOrder is invoked directly from learningOrderProvider's FutureProvider.family build callback, yet it performs a DB write (_stampReorderAt) whenever the stored learningOrderVersion is stale — and nothing else ever updates learningOrderVersion except an explicit user reorder/reset. So on every cold start or provider invalidation while the version mismatch persists, merely reading the curriculum's order silently re-stamps lastReorderAt = now, which is exactly the reorder-amnesty trigger — overdue-item detection for that curriculum stays silently suppressed after any content reseed until the user happens to manually reorder or reset, defeating a named product invariant via a function that looks like a pure read.
recommendation: Move the version-mismatch re-amnesty write out of getOrder into an explicit, one-shot repair step (run once at app start or as part of the content-reseed pipeline) so provider build stays a pure read.
acceptance_criteria: Test: call getOrder() twice in a row with a stale learningOrderVersion and assert lastReorderAt is stamped at most once, not on every call
Provider build functions in learning_order_providers.dart contain no DB write calls
